items.rawSummary: A Ukrainian drone struck the Mosfilm Tower near the Kremlin, part of an escalating series of attacks on Moscow that included over 200 drones and a cruise missile hit on a military plant, while security fears prompted Russia to scale back its Victory Day parade and ISW corroborated enhanced protective measures around senior officials.
items.analysis: Ukrainian drone activity escalated over consecutive nights in Moscow, with a suicide drone hitting the Mosfilm Tower just 6 km from the Kremlin, followed by a massive salvo of over 200 attack drones. Russian KA-52 attack helicopters were observed engaging drones over the city, and a Ukrainian Flamingo heavy cruise missile struck the VNIIR-Progress military electronics plant, a defense facility. These strikes coincide with President Zelensky’s warning that Ukrainian drones could reach the May 9 Victory Day parade, which Russia announced would exclude military equipment for the first time in years—citing financial pressure and fear of drone attacks. CNN reported that Western intelligence services assess a serious possibility of a coup attempt against Putin, with Kremlin security tightened and top generals placed under surveillance, while an EU-sanctioned general was appointed to lead Russia’s Aerospace Forces. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) has observed corroborating evidence of enhanced security measures for Putin and senior officials, including the reported movement of Pantsir-S1 and S-400 air defense systems near Putin’s residences since mid-2023, and noted a pattern of assassinations and attempts credited to Ukraine.

keyPoints.point: Russia says it will receive approximately $2.7 billion in extra revenue from higher oil prices.
Ukraine says its drone forces destroyed 38 Russian air defense targets worth about $1.1 billion in April to weaken defenses for deeper attacks.
Explosions were reported in Moscow, and a large emergency response was underway.
A Ukrainian suicide drone reportedly struck the Mosfilm Tower in central Moscow, located 6 km from the Kremlin.
The attack on Mosfilm Tower is reported to be the third consecutive night of drone activity in Moscow.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia announced a May 9 military parade in Moscow without military equipment, citing unaffordability and fear of drone attacks.
CNN reported that Western intelligence services assess a serious possibility of a coup in Russia against Putin, with security around the Kremlin tightened and top generals placed under surveillance.
An EU-sanctioned general was appointed head of Russia’s Aerospace Forces, succeeding Viktor Afzalov, amid ongoing investigations into his alleged role in civilian killings in Bucha.
Over 200 strike drones were reportedly launched by Ukraine toward Moscow.
Russian KA-52 attack helicopters were seen engaging a wide range of drones over Moscow.
A Ukrainian Flamingo heavy cruise missile struck Russia's VNIIR-Progress military electronics plant.

ISW reported corroborating evidence of enhanced security measures for Putin and senior Russian officials, including the movement of Pantsir-S1 and S-400 systems near Putin’s residences, and noted a pattern of assassinations and attempts credited to Ukraine.

items.rawSummary: Following an IRGC attack and possible detention of a bulk carrier near Sirik, US forces under Project Freedom destroyed Iranian small craft threatening shipping, while Iran warned of ceasefire violations if the US Navy enters the Strait of Hormuz.
items.analysis: The UKMTO reported a bulk carrier was attacked by multiple small craft 11 nautical miles west of Sirik, with all crew safe; Iran’s Fars News Agency claimed a vessel was detained for ignoring warnings, though it remains unclear if this was the same incident. The Institute for the Study of War assessed the IRGC Navy likely attacked the Liberian-flagged Minoan Falcon to sustain high shipping costs and oil prices as leverage against the United States. In response, President Trump announced ‘Project Freedom’ to guide neutral ships without Navy escorts and warned of force against interference, while Iranian officials threatened to treat any US intervention as a ceasefire violation and ordered the US Navy to stay out of the strait. Concurrently, a tanker north of Fujairah was struck by IRGC projectiles and ships near Ras Al Khaimah received VHF orders to leave anchorage, escalating regional tensions. CENTCOM subsequently reported that US Navy MH-60 Sea Hawks and Army AH-64 Apaches destroyed Iranian small boats threatening commercial shipping under the Project Freedom operation, marking a direct military engagement.
items.locationName: Strait of Hormuz, west of Sirik, Hormozgan Province

keyPoints.point: UK Maritime Trade Operations reported a bulk carrier attacked by multiple small craft off Sirik, Iran, with crew safe and advised vessels to proceed with caution.
A large cargo ship was reportedly attacked by multiple small craft near the Strait of Hormuz off Sirik, Iran.
UKMTO specified the incident location was 21 nautical miles west of Sirik, Iran.
UKMTO indicated that IRGC forces appeared to have attacked the vessel as it transited the Strait of Hormuz.
UKMTO revised the incident location to 11 nautical miles west of Sirik, Iran.

Iran’s Fars News Agency reported that a vessel was detained near Sirik for ignoring warnings from the Iranian Armed Forces, without confirming if it was the same vessel as the bulk carrier earlier reported attacked.

The Institute for the Study of War assessed that the IRGC Navy likely attacked the Liberian-flagged, Greek-owned Minoan Falcon, which turned south after the attack, as a tactic to pressure the US by sustaining high shipping costs and oil prices.
Ships near Ras Al Khaimah, UAE received VHF orders to leave anchorage.

items.rawSummary: JNIM launches offensive in northern Mali
items.analysis: JNIM, an Al-Qaeda affiliated group, launched an offensive in northern Mali on April 25, described as historic. The operation marks a significant escalation in militant activity in the Sahel region. The Critical Threats Project scheduled a discussion to assess implications for the United States. The offensive threatens stability in an already insecure area.

items.rawSummary: Large fire at the Arghvan shopping center in Andisheh, west of Tehran.
items.analysis: A large fire broke out at the Arghvan shopping center in Andisheh, west of Tehran, according to Fars News and Tasnim News. The cause of the blaze remains unknown, and firefighters were deployed to the scene. No casualty figures have been released.
